notes_markdown:
**culler now tells you when there's a new culler** — plus a batch of
fixes and polish straight from the same live-server field session.

- **Update notice.** On launch, culler makes a single anonymous HTTPS
  request to GitHub for a small version file (at most once a day — no
  account, telemetry, or usage data). When a newer version exists, a
  quiet `● update vX.Y.Z` note joins the corner readout and an
  "Update available" item joins the Help menu; clicking either opens
  the release notes in your browser. Nothing pops up, nothing installs
  itself, and if you're offline the check fails silently. Add
  `disabled=1` to `~/.culler/update.conf` to turn it off.
- **Server exports now match your screen.** On an Immich source, `J`
  for a RAW+JPEG pair used to render the camera JPEG with your slider
  values — not the RAW render the develop panel was showing — so the
  uploaded picture could look different from what you graded. The
  export now bakes the same full RAW demosaic the panel shows, and a
  new server round-trip test proves the uploaded file is byte-for-byte
  what was rendered.
- **Re-uploading a pair can't double its stack.** When part of a pair
  is already on the server (say the RAW, from an earlier upload), a new
  upload now joins the existing stack — newest JPEG in front, old
  members kept — instead of creating a second stack over the same
  photo. Re-running an already-finished batch changes nothing at all.
- **"Some photos didn't load" now says why.** When timeline pages fail
  to load from a server, the warning names the failed pages and the
  server's actual error instead of only a count — and each failure is
  also logged to the console (look for `culler: scan:` lines in
  Console.app), so a recurring problem can actually be diagnosed.
- **The manual shows real photographs.** Every screenshot in the
  [manual](https://mertenssander.github.io/culler-releases/manual/) is
  reshot with real RAW+JPEG pairs instead of generated test images.
